content.title: Gold Strike Park
content.summary: The City of Arvada has completed the final site plan for Gold Strike Park, which includes features such as a Montane Nesting Forest, Wetland Boardwalk, and a Prairie Dog Bicycle Playground. Construction is expected to begin in summer 2026 and be completed by fall 2028, following a collaborative consultation process with the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes to integrate indigenous perspectives into the park's design. The project aims to restore ecosystems, strengthen community connections, and honor the land's historical significance.

## Latest Project Updates

1. [Final Site Plan Complete and Next Steps](#tabf7e3e047-bd50-41a2-b427-8fa7f4622611_0)

With construction documentation now complete, the City of Arvada is excited to share the final site plan for Gold Strike Park! [View an enlarged image of the site plan](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=6559).[![Gold Strike Park site map showing: parking, meadows, creek, bike playground, pavilions, lawns, boardwalk.](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6559)](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=6559)

The final site features:

- Montane Nesting Forest
- Wetland Boardwalk
- Riparian Beaver Lodge
- Grasslands Buffalo Herd
- Prairie Dog Bicycle Playground
- New education and picnic pavilions
- Pedestrian bridge, and connections to the regional trail system.

The park’s restored meadows, nesting habitats, and interpretive art will make it both a recreational destination and a place for reflection.

### Next Steps in the project

The project recently received approval through the City’s development review process, with bidding and procurement to follow before year’s end barring any unforeseen complications.

Construction is anticipated to begin in summer 2026, marked by a ground-blessing ceremony, and reach completion by fall 2028.

Through ongoing collaboration, thoughtful design, and national recognition, the Gold Strike Park project continues to reflect Arvada’s commitment to building spaces that restore ecosystems, strengthen community connections, and honor the stories that shape our shared landscape.

**Project timeline at a glance**

- Grant agreement: March 2026
- Bidding and procurement: April-May 2026
- Construction start & ground blessing: Summer 2026
- Project completion: Fall 2028

1. [Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes Consultation](#tabf7e3e047-bd50-41a2-b427-8fa7f4622611_1)

The City of Arvada is proud to share an important step in the Gold Strike Park redevelopment project: a multi-day consultation with the [Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes](https://www.cheyenneandarapaho-nsn.gov/). This partnership reflects the City’s commitment to inclusive, respectful, and historically grounded public projects that honor the original stewards of this land.

The relationship between the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes and the City of Arvada began in July 2023 with the naming of [Little Raven Park](/868). The two organizations continued to build their collaborative relationship in the two years since then.

In June 2025, the City welcomed Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribal Historian Gordon Yellowman and other tribal representatives to Arvada for a multi-day visit focused on cultural consultation and shared visioning for the design of Gold Strike Park. Hosted by the City’s Parks and Urban Design Department, the visit centered on storytelling, knowledge-sharing, and relationship-building, with the goal of integrating indigenous perspectives and traditions into the future of the park.

This collaboration is not just symbolic — it’s foundational. The design process for Gold Strike Park recognizes the significance of the land to indigenous peoples and the importance of addressing generational trauma of the land and its people through healing, education, and trust-building. Through this partnership, tribal representatives are helping shape a park that reflects both the historical truths and future hopes of all communities.

The City recently finalized an Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) with the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes that outlines the scope of services and ensures the City reimburses the Tribes for all associated expenses. The agreement was formally approved by the Arvada City Council on July 1, 2025.

Chief Yellowman will also be joining members of the Gold Strike Park design team to present at the American Society of Landscape Architects (ASLA) annual national conference in October. The title of their presentation is “Listening to the Land: Integrating Indigenous Perspectives for Restoration and Healing.”

The City is deeply honored to work alongside the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes in this process, and looks forward to co-creating a space at Gold Strike Park that serves as a place of reflection, reconnection, and celebration for generations to come.

![Three people walk along a paved trail toward a cable-stayed bridge with trees around.](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6074)

1. [Gold Strike Park Awarded $750K grant from Great Outdoors Colorado](#tabf7e3e047-bd50-41a2-b427-8fa7f4622611_2)

![Great Outdoors Colorado (GOCO) Logo ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6075)On March 13, 2025, [Great Outdoors Colorado (GOCO)](https://goco.org/) announced that the Gold Strike Park project has been awarded a $750,000 grant as part of its Community Impact program.

"We are incredibly grateful to GOCO for this generous grant, which will help bring the vision for Gold Strike Park to life," said Ryan Stevenson, the City of Arvada's Director of Vibrant Community and Neighborhoods. "Transforming this underutilized site into a vibrant and inclusive green space requires strong partnerships, and GOCO's support is instrumental in making that happen. This investment ensures that the park will serve as both a historical landmark and a welcoming recreational destination for the community for generations to come."

Read more about the grant and the Community Impact program from [GOCO's press release.](https://goco.org/news/releases/goco-awards-79m-for-parks-planning-and-conservation)

1. [Gold Strike Park featured on Inside Arvada podcast](#tabf7e3e047-bd50-41a2-b427-8fa7f4622611_3)

Senior Landscape Architect and project manager Maki Boyle was a guest on the City of Arvada's Inside Arvada podcast on Jan. 22. You can listen to the podcast episode using the player below, or on [Apple](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/inside-gold-strike-park-with-maki-boyle/id1736238466?i=1000685009431), [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/6iqPbu9uqv3aADoWy4wDwC?si=rEIwkfqSRoWLJ7za1zRkQw), [YouTube](https://youtu.be/YRo2vgiHDto?si=0WIif5yXVx6ylctH) or [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/16454557) (transcript available).

1. [Arvada Selected to Receive $7.3M in Federal Grant Funding](#tabf7e3e047-bd50-41a2-b427-8fa7f4622611_4)

![Logos for the National Park Service, Land and Water Conservation Fund, U.S. Department of the Interior](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=6076)

On Sept. 25, 2024, it was announced that the City of Arvada has been selected to receive $7.3 million in funding through the Outdoor Recreation Legacy Partnership (ORLP) grant program for the transformation of Gold Strike Park

[Read more about the ORLP grant](https://www.arvadaco.gov/CivicAlerts.aspx?AID=174&ARC=527).

1. [Preferred Schematic Design](#tabf7e3e047-bd50-41a2-b427-8fa7f4622611_5)

The City of Arvada is excited to present the [preferred schematic site design report for Gold Strike Park (PDF)](/DocumentCenter/View/3083).

[Watch a presentation by the project team to learn more about the schematic design process](https://youtu.be/LVMQMJjqpYY?feature=shared).

Using feedback we received from multiple rounds of community engagement in 2023, the final plan includes the following elements:

- Natural splash area
- Nature play
- Flexible event lawn
- Educational pavilion
- Creek overlooks
- Bouldering feature
- Wetland boardwalk and overlook

The final plan for Gold Strike Park includes two options, with the difference being which element is featured in the southeast corner of the park:

- [Option A - Bicycle Playground](/DocumentCenter/View/3118/Gold-Strike-Park-Final-Plan-Option-A---Bicycle-Playground)
- [Option B - Dog Park or Community Garden](/DocumentCenter/View/3119/Gold-Strike-Park-Final-Plan-Option-B---Dog-Park-or-Community-Garden)

## Project Overview

Gold Strike Park sits at the confluence of Clear Creek and Ralston Creek in the City of Arvada and is listed on the State Registrar of Historical Places as the site where gold was first documented in Colorado. Efforts to turn the 7.6-acre site into a community space for historical and ecological explorations began more than 45 years ago. The city has launched a park design effort to fulfill Gold Strike Park's full potential as the next great park for Arvada. The park design effort builds on the [2019 Clear Creek Corridor Plan (PDF)](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=68cc27b9c7ef8), the [2016 Parks, Trails, and Open Space Master Plan (PDF)](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=68c0b26db9532), and the [2000 Gold Strike Park Master Plan (PDF)](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/munidocs/munidocs?nodeId=68cc2abfae699).

![Gold Strike Park Base Map showing the park off of 56th avenue and ralston road, just west of Sheridan Blvd](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=624)

## Community Engagement

This project builds on previous planning recommendations and community input. Community engagement activities that took place in 2023 further informed the development of a design for Gold Strike Park. Engagement began with collecting community input on ideas and a vision for the park in early 2023, followed by design alternatives presented back to the public for feedback in the summer.

A final schematic design was presented in February 2024.
